To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the absence of sperm in the SCOS is due to the congenital (intrinsic) or secondary (acquired) form, and that the congenital form can be predicted by histology and immunohistochemistry.
the two different histological patterns, congenital and secondary SCOS, are characterized by different prognosis for sperm recovery and different endocrinologic and genetic background.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new criteria predicting the absence of germinal cells in the testis, in order to reduce sperm retrieval failure during TESE and to avoid unnecessary ovarian stimulation of the spouse in ICSI programmes.
the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies in male infertility, with special regard to non-obstructive zoospermia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in order to achieve a successful sperm recovery by testicular biopsy, a definite diagnosis of SCOS is mandatory.
a definite recognition of both histological patterns of the SCOS, together with the application of the above mentioned diagnostic aids, would improve success rates in sperm retrieval during TESE.

a definite recognition of SCOS patterns can be obtained by diagnostic testicular biopsy, and that the use of endocrine, chemical and molecular biology aids can be of great help in refining the diagnosis of congenital versus secondary SCOS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diagnosis of congenital SCOS is the most reliable method to avoid sperm retrieval failure and ovarian stimulation of patients' spouses in the case of non-obstructive zoospermia.
, in the presence of SCOS, the diagnosis of congenital SCOS is a strong indication to avoid ovarian stimulation of the female partner and to consider alternative methods to achieve pregnancy.

, in order to increase the efficacy of TE SE in the treatment of non-obstructive zoospermia, the histological diagnosis of SCOS should be performed by an expert in this field, and the diagnostic testicular biopsies should be performed by experienced surgeons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnosis of the two histological patterns of Sertoli cell only syndrome can be refined by the use of endocrine, chemical and molecular biology aids and by immunohistochemistry.
the diagnosis of the two histological patterns is crucial to predict the absence or the presence of spermatozo in the testis of patients with non-obstrucive azoosperemia.
the diagnosis of congenital and acquired SCOS can improve the efficacy of TESES in ICSI programmes.
